classification.difficultyReason: Form surface-area equations from labelled dimensions; the hardest part multiplies algebraic lengths, collects squared terms and selects the positive square root for a length.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The surface area of this rectangular prism is $376\text{ cm}^2$. Work out the value of $x$.

spec.description: Unshaded rectangular prism showing top, front and left faces. Dimension arrows follow the left receding base edge, front base edge and right vertical edge.
spec.mathematics: The three perpendicular dimensions are 6 cm, 10 cm and x cm; surface area is 376 cm².
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; no solved value of x.

children.prompt: Work out the value of $x$ in each of these rectangular prisms.

spec.description: Long unshaded rectangular prism with top, long side and right end visible. The 16 m arrow follows the long receding edge, 3 m the right vertical edge and x m the short base of the right end.
spec.mathematics: The perpendicular dimensions are 16 m, 3 m and x m; surface area is 248 m².
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; no solved value of x.

spec.description: Unshaded rectangular prism showing top, left side and front face. Algebraic dimension arrows follow the left receding base edge, front base edge and right vertical edge.
spec.mathematics: The perpendicular dimensions are 6x cm, 2x cm and x cm; surface area is 90 cm².
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; no solved value of x.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}90&=2(6x\times2x)+2(6x\times x)+2(2x\times x)\\90&=24x^2+12x^2+4x^2\\90&=40x^2\\x^2&=2.25\\x&=1.5\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Take the positive root because $x$ is a length.
